findings.reason: the section should cite OperatorRequestKind and be written as extending fixed_point.py's machine (or say why that machine cannot carry the whole-solve body), which changes both its wording and its scope.
findings.text: the §3 design paragraph says "the section implements one lax state machine whose sole operator body serves residual, merit, acceptance, recovery, reconciliation and Jacobian-vector requests", but nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py already defines exactly that: OperatorRequestKind (fixed_point.py:923) enumerates the acceptance/recovery/reconciliation/merit kinds and the request serve machine (lax.switch + lax.scan loop at fixed_point.py:995-1041, served at fixed_point.py:2403-2407) — the section reads as building a subsystem that exists, so a fresh implementer cannot tell it is extending the committed machine rather than forking a parallel one

findings.reason: the section must name cache_reuse_summary.py:63 served_keys as the owner to reuse and state which of the two existing served_entries sites it retires or repairs, otherwise the guard and the summariser diverge on the same number.
findings.text: §4 asks to "make the guard's served_entries count program-key cache entries rather than a recursive file count", but the program-key counting it describes already exists as served_keys() in scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py:63, which is exactly how that module reports "served_entries": len(disk) at cache_reuse_summary.py:115; served_entries itself is already computed at two sites (cache_guard.py:209 directory_entry_count and prewarm.sh:135 find|wc -l), so §4 risks adding a third program-key counter rather than reconciling the two existing ones

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan consolidates behaviour onto one scan body (§2) and one traced operator body (§3) rather than adding shallow wrappers, and proposes no new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's program-key served_entries duplicates the existing program-key counting owner scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds to any of these families, so nothing must be retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1/§2/§4 cite the machinery they extend (the four committed route files and dd7d8286; the memory gate beside the new size gate; the pre-warm pin and cache guard), but §3's design paragraph proposes "one lax state machine" without citing nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py, which already carries precisely that machine.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the changes are in-place extensions of existing machinery (the request machine, the size gate, the pre-warm counter), not a new layer over it.
